title: Exact propagating Dirac wave packets in an attractive Coulomb-like potential
abstract: We construct exact, positive-energy, normalizable wave-packet solutions of the Dirac equation in the axisymmetric potential $V=-\,v_0/ρ$ -- to our knowledge, the first such solutions in any external potential. Remarkably, one family comprises only elementary functions whose longitudinal profiles reproduce the free-Schrödinger Hermite--Gauss wave packets in the nonrelativistic limit. All packets share two striking features: (i) a probability density that is pointwise decoupled from spin orientation -- despite the inherent spin-orbit coupling of the Dirac equation -- and (ii) a complete freezing of their time evolution at the critical coupling $v_0\to\hbar c/2$. We also present a simple scheme that maps solutions of the 2D Helmholtz equation to further exact Dirac wave packets.
summary: This paper presents the construction of exact, propagating wave-packet solutions for the Dirac equation in an attractive Coulomb-like potential. The key findings include demonstrating that the probability density decouples from spin and that the wave packet's time evolution freezes at a critical coupling strength. This provides significant analytical insight into relativistic quantum dynamics in structured potentials.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing exact, positive-energy, normalizable wave-packet solutions for the Dirac equation subjected to an attractive Coulomb-like potential ($V = -v_0/ho$).
main_result: The authors constructed novel families of exact solutions exhibiting two key features: spin-density decoupling and temporal freezing at a critical coupling. These solutions correctly reduce to known nonrelativistic forms like the Hermite–Gauss wave packet.
method: Methods involve solving coupled partial differential equations derived from the Dirac Hamiltonian, utilizing superposition techniques, and mapping solutions from the 2D Helmholtz equation (H->D map).
model_or_system: The model is the relativistic Dirac equation solved in cylindrical coordinates with a central potential $V = -v_0/ho$. The analysis focuses on propagating wave packets characterized by their longitudinal marginal density.
key_observables: Longitudinal marginal density $P(z, t)$, spin-density decoupling ($\Psi^\dagger\Psi$ independent of spin), and the group velocity's slowing down as confinement increases.
important_parameters: The coupling constant $v_0$, which has a critical value leading to temporal freezing; the nonrelativistic limit ($c 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially sets $\hbar=m=c=1$ and focuses on positive-energy eigenstates. The derivation relies on symmetry considerations for axisymmetric Hamiltonians.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the time evolution of the marginal density showing dispersive spreading that slows down as confinement increases, leading to temporal freezing. Figure 2 shows this effect for varying coupling parameters.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives solutions by first establishing the governing PDEs, providing explicit examples using elementary functions, and later developing a general mapping scheme (H->D) from known solvable equations like the Helmholtz equation.
why_interesting: This work provides exact analytical solutions for wave propagation in a confining potential within a relativistic framework, which is highly relevant to understanding particle confinement in structured media or quantum waveguides beyond simple approximations.
